participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novibs main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fund raising, campaigning and advocacy. The Hub Niamey Niger exists since 2006 as a humanitarian field office and since 2012 as the decentralized Country office for Oxfam Novib, dealing with all the development and humanitarian themes like Sustainable livelihoods, Right to Basic services, Humanitarian and resilience interventions, The right to be heard and the right to an Identity, including women's rights and sexual and reproductive health rights. The Country Office in Niger works with local partners to realize the vision of a Niger without poverty

comment.narrative: Réseau des Jeunes Nigériens sur le Changement Climatique (RJNCC); Jeunes Volontaires pour l’Environnement – Niger (JVE-Niger); Agence Nationale de Financement des Collectivités Territoriales (ANFICT); Association des Municipalités du Niger (AMN); the Ministry of Environment, Hydraulics and Sanitation (MEH/A); the Services Techniques Décentralisés (STD); the Communes de Maradi; and participating Climate Activists. These actors include civil society organizations and youth climate networks, national government institutions, local government associations, and international partners collaborating to support awareness-raising, policy engagement, and the revision process of Niger’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC).

comment.narrative: The organizations and institutions collaborated through several joint actions aimed at supporting climate governance and the revision of Niger’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0). Excluding the funder, the collaboration involved the following key actions:1. Co-organization of the awareness and mobilization workshopThe Ministry of Environment, Hydraulics and Sanitation (MEH/A), the Nigerien Youth Network on Climate Change (RJNCC), and Young Volunteers for the Environment–Niger (JVE-Niger) jointly organized and facilitated a workshop in Maradi to inform and mobilize local authorities and stakeholders on climate change and the NDC revision process.2. Engagement of local government institutionsThe Association of Municipalities of Niger (AMN), the National Agency for the Financing of Local Authorities (ANFICT), municipal authorities from the Communes of Maradi, and Decentralized Technical Services (STD) participated in discussions aimed at integrating climate change considerations into municipal planning and development processes.3. Development of a commitment note for municipalitiesStakeholders collectively contributed to the preparation of a commitment note addressed to the 255 municipalities of Niger, encouraging them to integrate climate changeconsiderations into their annual and five-year development plans.4. Joint awareness and advocacy on climate policy Civil society organizations (RJNCC and JVE-Niger), together with government and municipal actors, collaborated to raise awareness about climate change, mobilize communities and local authorities, and strengthen advocacy around the NDC revision process.5. Strengthening climate-sensitive local planning Partners agreed to support municipalities in integrating climate change into Communal Development Plans (PDCs) and local investment plans through capacity building, technical guidance, and the promotion of climate-sensitive planning approaches.
